_readme: WO-74 — the dress-hire shelf. Asked by Nan 2026-09-07 off a search for
"thai clothing rentals photoshoot" that returned som tam, noodles and a
pharmacy chain, with the line: I'm pretty sure the information is
available to us, but tags and discoverability not there.
It was available. WO-49 read all 38 of CMHY's rental houses on 2026-08-31
into data/curated/tailor.json — GPS, phone, hashtags, the directory's own
last-updated date — and 4 of them became records. The other 34 sat in a
research file no page reads. This file admits them, on a shelf of their
own, with the English words that make them reachable.
FOUR TRADES, ONE ENGLISH PHRASE. A gown-and-uniform house is not an
answer to a Lanna-costume question and a cabaret costumier is not an
answer to a wedding, so the strands are kept apart and every shop is
The price bands below are quoted to their sources and unverified — nobody here has hired a costume. The
nine shops CMHY marks 'may have closed or moved' are carried with that
sentence attached, not deleted: a directory note is not a closure.

corpus.note_en: The gap was never a gap in the corpus. Thirty-four shops with pins and phone numbers were unreachable by any search, on any shelf, in the API and on the map, because nothing had ever carried them out of a research file.
corpus.note_th: ข้อมูลมีอยู่แล้ว ร้านเช่าชุด 34 ร้านพร้อมพิกัดและเบอร์โทรอยู่ในไฟล์วิจัย ไม่เคยถูกนำออกมาเป็นรายการ จึงค้นไม่เจอทั้งในเว็บ ในแผนที่ และใน API

words.note: Noise, and worse than noise: ถ่าย ('to take a photograph') romanises to THAI under RTGS, so the reading of ถ่ายภาพ is 'Thai Phap' and every photo studio in the corpus matches the word 'thai' for a reason that has nothing to do with Thailand.
The thesaurus has no group for `dress`. Ban Or Jao's English is 'Thai dress hire', so the reader's word never reached it.
`rent`/`rental`/`hire`/`เช่า` ARE one thesaurus group — but the group is the CAR one, and every rental house in this file was off the shelf it would have ranked on.

Zero in the corpus, zero in the thesaurus. The rarest word is the question (go/guitar-bug); here the rarest word was also the unanswerable one, so the AND collapsed and the page fell back to ranking on 'thai'.

thesaurus_gaps_found: `costume` — no group at all, 2 records anywhere
ชุด (an outfit, a set) is grouped with `suite` and `unit` — a hotel word

words.note_en: The gloss column is what makes a Thai-only tag findable in English. Before this file the four Lanna-costume studios carried ถ่ายภาพชุดล้านนา with NO gloss, so the index held the Thai and the reading 'Thai Phap Chutlanna' and nothing an English speaker would ever type.

venues.note_en: Where people actually wear it. No stall here is a record: nobody has read a shop's name off these pavements, so there is no pin. Listed because the trade is not only the shops with doors.

rows.th: วัดต้นเกว๋น (วัดอินทราวาส) ต.หนองควาย อ.หางดง
rows.en: Wat Ton Kwen (Wat Inthrawat), Nong Khwai, Hang Dong
rows.what_en: Costume stalls at the lane mouth and in front of the temple. Thai-language reviews from 2025 and 2026 put a Lanna outfit at about 150 baht with hair and jewellery included, and a photographer as a separate half-hour add-on. The temple became the city's costume-photograph place after the drama กลิ่นกาสะลอง was filmed there.

rows.th: วัดในเวียง — วัดเจดีย์หลวง วัดพระสิงห์ ประตูท่าแพ
rows.en: The old-city temples — Wat Chedi Luang, Wat Phra Singh, Tha Phae Gate
rows.what_en: Where the packaged trade shoots. Booking platforms list Chiang Mai costume-and-photographer packages from about 450–490 baht for the outfit with dressing and accessories, half-day or full-day, with a photographer and make-up as add-ons and two days' notice asked for the photographer.

rows.th: ตลาดวโรรส (กาดหลวง) — ผ้าและชุดพื้นเมือง
rows.en: Warorot Market (Kat Luang) — cloth and northern dress
rows.what_en: The cloth end of the same trade: local cotton, phasin and ready-made northern dress sold rather than hired, upstairs in the market. Named here because a reader who wants to OWN one is asking a different question from a reader who wants one for an afternoon.

prices.note_en: Quoted to whoever published them. Three price worlds sit in one trade and a reader shown only one of them draws the wrong conclusion — the same finding WO-49 recorded for gown hire.

refused.what_en: Naming a best costume-hire in Chiang Mai.
refused.why_en: WO-49's rule, and it holds harder here: every English 'top ten' page in this trade is a booking platform's own inventory.

refused.what_en: Declaring the nine 'may have closed' shops closed.
refused.why_en: That is CMHY's own note asking readers to correct it, not a finding. It is carried with its Thai wording attached. Absence of evidence is not evidence of absence.

refused.what_en: Giving the Wat Ton Kwen stalls names, pins or records.
refused.why_en: The trade there is well attested and no stall's own name has been read. A venue with citations is honest; six invented pins would not be.

refused.what_en: Putting any price on a place record.
refused.why_en: Nobody here has hired a costume. The prices are quoted and flagged unverified.

refused.what_en: Offering a gown-and-uniform house as an answer to a Lanna-dress question.
refused.why_en: Four trades, one English phrase. Kept apart, as WO-49 kept the four tailoring trades apart.

unread.name: cm-osm-node-624114779 vs cm-onab-03501509003
unread.reason: The same temple twice — วัดต้นเกว๋น from OSM at 18.7228/98.9253, วัดอินทราวาส from the ONAB register at 18.7374/98.9151, which is the pin of a pharmacy 1.6 km away. Neither record carries the other's name, so half the readers looking for this temple find a record that cannot tell them they have arrived. Found here, not fixed here — it belongs with the shared-pin work.
